title: OCG: Optical Character Grounded Visual Reasoning with Flow Matching
abstract: Multimodal systems typically couple a vision encoder with a language model, relying on cross-attention or projection layers to bridge heterogeneous token spaces. We ask a different question: can a pure vision generation model, operating entirely in RGB pixel space, perform visual reasoning? We propose OCG (Optical Character Grounded Visual Reasoning), a framework in which both the input question and output answer are rendered as text images, and a vision-only generative model replaces autoregressive text decoding with flow-matching generation in pixel space, without any sample-specific text conditioning. Since optical characters carry the same information as their text-token equivalents, this unified RGB representation may reduce the cross-modal alignment burden. A dual-teacher self-distillation scheme transfers the pretrained model’s existing reasoning and generation capabilities into the new image-to-image pathway, and off-the-shelf OCR converts generated answer images back to text for evaluation on standard benchmarks. Experiments on CLEVR show that our dual-teacher distillation substantially outperforms fine-tuning without distillation or with single-teacher distillation, suggesting that flow matching in image space offers a viable path toward unifying language reasoning, understanding, and generation in RGB space.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Welcome to Advanced Topics in Multimodal AI. Today's lecture is on a fascinating paper titled 'OCG: Optical Character Grounded Visual Reasoning with Flow Matching.' We've recently seen a push towards unifying modalities, with works like 'FlowTok' projecting text and images into a shared latent space. This paper from researchers at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China takes a more radical approach.
segments.zh: 欢迎来到多模态AI进阶专题。今天我们要讲的是一篇很有意思的论文，题目叫“OCG：基于光流匹配的光学字符锚定视觉推理”。最近我们看到有一股统一不同模态的趋势，比如FlowTok这项工作就是把文本和图像投影到一个共享的潜空间里。而这篇来自电子科技大学研究人员的论文走了一条更激进的路子。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It questions the very necessity of separate token spaces by operating entirely within the RGB pixel domain. It proposes a pure vision model can handle these tasks. Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 它质疑了独立token空间的必要性，因为它完全在RGB像素域内运作。它提出纯视觉模型就能处理这些任务。好，诺亚？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Excuse me, Professor. So, are they suggesting we can just get rid of text tokenizers and language models for visual reasoning tasks? That seems counterintuitive.
segments.zh: 不好意思，教授。那他们是在说，对于视觉推理任务，我们可以直接不要文本token分词器和语言模型了吗？这听起来有点反直觉。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In a sense, yes, at least during the core reasoning phase. The motivation is to reduce the architectural complexity inherent in standard Vision-Language Models. Think of the projection layers and cross-attention mechanisms needed to bridge visual tokens and text tokens. OCG investigates whether we can bypass that 'alignment tax' by unifying everything into a single representation space: pixels.
segments.zh: 从某种意义上说，是的，至少在核心推理阶段是这样。这么做是为了降低标准视觉语言模型固有的架构复杂度。想想那些用来连接视觉token和文本token的投影层和交叉注意力机制。OCG要研究的是，我们能不能通过把所有东西统一到一种表示空间——像素——来绕过这种“对齐税”。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The core idea is to reformulate visual reasoning as an image-to-image translation problem. You take your scene image, and you literally paste a rendered image of the text question below it. This becomes your input image. The model's job is to generate a new image where the question part is replaced by a rendered image of the answer. All reasoning happens as a pixel-to-pixel transformation.
segments.zh: 核心思路是把视觉推理重新表述成一个图像到图像的翻译问题。你拿到场景图像，然后把文字问题渲染成一张图，直接贴在它下面。这就成了你的输入图像。模型的任务是生成一张新图像，其中问题部分被替换成渲染后的答案图像。所有的推理都以像素到像素的变换形式发生。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: But doesn't representing text as pixels feel incredibly inefficient? You're adding so much redundant information compared to a discrete token.
segments.zh: 但把文本表示成像素，是不是感觉效率特别低？跟离散的token比起来，你多塞了太多冗余信息进去。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's a critical point, and the authors acknowledge it. This isn't proposed as a replacement for language decoders in general-purpose tasks due to that inefficiency. Rather, it serves as a powerful diagnostic tool. It asks: can a model that only sees and produces pixels learn to perform complex, compositional reasoning? The surprising answer they find is yes, to a high degree.
segments.zh: 这点很关键，作者自己也承认了。正因效率不高，他们并不是想用它来取代通用任务里的语言解码器，而是把它当作一个强大的诊断工具。它要问的是：一个只看像素、也只生成像素的模型，能不能学会做复杂的组合式推理？他们得到的答案出人意料：能，而且在很大程度上可以。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So how do they actually get the model to do this? The base model must have some language understanding to start with, right?
segments.zh: 那他们到底是怎么让模型做到这一点的呢？基础模型一开始肯定得具备一定的语言理解能力吧？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. They build on a strong pretrained unified model called SenseNova-U1. Crucially, they found that this model couldn't perform the task in a zero-shot setting. If you just gave it the input image and asked for an answer image, it would fail, often generating garbled text or parts of the instructions. This is where their main technical contribution comes in: a dual-teacher self-distillation scheme.
segments.zh: 没错。他们是在一个强大的预训练统一模型 SenseNova-U1 的基础上做的。关键在于，他们发现这个模型在零样本设置下根本完不成这个任务。如果你直接把输入图像给它，让它生成一张答案图像，它会失败，经常生成乱码文字或者指令里的某些片段。这就引出了他们的主要技术贡献：一种双教师自蒸馏方案。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: A dual-teacher scheme? Can you elaborate on that?
segments.zh: 双教师方案？能详细讲讲吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Certainly. During fine-tuning, they run three parallel paths. The first is Teacher 1, which uses the model’s native image-plus-text-to-text path. It takes the scene image and the actual question string to generate the text answer. This path's internal states, specifically the key-value or KV states, capture the reasoning process.
segments.zh: 当然可以。在微调过程中，他们会并行运行三条路径。第一条是教师1，走的是模型原生的图像加文本到文本的路径。它接收场景图像和实际问题字符串，生成文本答案。这条路径的内部状态，具体来说是键值状态，也就是KV状态，捕捉了推理过程。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Teacher 2 uses the text-to-image path. It takes the ground-truth answer string and generates KV states that represent the condition for rendering that specific answer. Finally, you have the student path, which is the image-to-image pipeline they want to train. The student's internal KV states are forced to align with the teachers' states using a loss function. Early layers are left to learn visual features, middle layers are aligned with the reasoning teacher, and final layers are aligned with the generation teacher.
segments.zh: 教师2走的是文本到图像的路径。它接收真实答案字符串，生成KV状态，这些状态代表了渲染该特定答案的条件。最后是学生路径，也就是他们想要训练的图像到图像流水线。学生的内部KV状态通过损失函数被强制与教师的状态对齐。浅层留给学习视觉特征，中间层与推理教师对齐，最后几层与生成教师对齐。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So it’s not learning to reason from scratch in pixel space. It's learning to mimic the internal reasoning and generation processes of its own pretrained pathways.
segments.zh: 所以它并不是从零开始在像素空间里学习推理，而是在学习模仿自己那些预训练路径内部的推理和生成过程。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Precisely. It's a method of knowledge transfer. You're teaching the image-only pathway how to replicate the behavior of the text-involved pathways. And the results are quite strong. On the CLEVR dataset, the OCG model achieved 94.6% accuracy, which is very close to the 98.1% they call the 'Oracle OCR' upper bound—the score you'd get if the model generated perfect images but still had to go through a standard OCR engine for evaluation.
segments.zh: 正是如此。这是一种知识迁移的方法。你在教纯图像通路如何复现那些涉及文本的通路的行为。而且结果相当强。在CLEVR数据集上，OCG模型达到了94.6%的准确率，非常接近他们称为“Oracle OCR”上限的98.1%——也就是模型生成完美图像、但仍需通过标准OCR引擎评估时能拿到的分数。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Wait, they use an OCR engine for evaluation? Doesn't that introduce another variable?
segments.zh: 等等，他们用OCR引擎来做评估？那不就引入了另一个变量吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It does, and it's a key limitation they discuss. The OCR is only used for evaluation, not during training. It converts the generated answer image back to text to score it. This means some errors could be from the OCR engine, not the model. However, the ablation studies are telling. When they removed the dual-teacher distillation and trained only on a pixel loss, accuracy plummeted to 50%. This shows that mimicking the internal reasoning states is what makes this work, not just matching pixels.
segments.zh: 确实有这个问题，而且这是他们讨论的一个关键局限。OCR只在评估阶段使用，训练时并不涉及。它的作用是把生成的答案图像转回文本，以便打分。这意味着有些错误可能来自OCR引擎，而不是模型本身。不过，消融实验很能说明问题。当他们去掉双教师蒸馏、只用像素损失训练时，准确率骤降到50%。这说明真正让这个方法奏效的是模仿内部推理状态，而不仅仅是匹配像素。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: This research really shifts the perspective. While other approaches like 'GRIT' or 'Machine Mental Imagery' try to better integrate visual information into a text-based reasoning chain—by interleaving text with bounding boxes or latent visual tokens—OCG goes in the opposite direction. It forces all information, including linguistic reasoning, into the visual modality. It suggests the modality boundary might be more fluid than our typical architectures assume.
segments.zh: 这项研究确实转变了视角。像GRIT或Machine Mental Imagery这些方法，试图把视觉信息更好地整合进基于文本的推理链里，比如把文本和边界框或潜在视觉token交错排列，而OCG反其道而行之。它把所有信息，包括语言推理，全都塞进视觉模态里。这说明模态之间的边界可能比我们通常的架构所假设的要模糊得多。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: How does this generalize beyond a synthetic dataset like CLEVR, though? Real-world images and questions are much messier.
segments.zh: 不过，这种方法在CLEVR这种合成数据集之外能泛化到什么程度呢？真实世界的图像和问题要混乱得多。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's the main open question. The authors are clear that this was tested on a constrained environment. Generalizing to more diverse datasets, handling longer answers, and mitigating the computational cost are all significant hurdles. But as a proof of concept, it's compelling. It demonstrates that the reasoning capabilities learned during language pretraining can be effectively transferred and executed entirely within a visual generation process, without discrete tokens at inference time.
segments.zh: 这确实是个核心的开放问题。作者也很清楚，这个实验是在一个受限环境中做的。要推广到更多样的数据集、处理更长的答案、降低计算成本，这些都是不小的障碍。但作为一个概念验证，它很有说服力。它表明，语言预训练阶段学到的推理能力，可以有效地迁移过来，完全在视觉生成过程中执行，推理时不需要离散的token。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: To wrap up, OCG presents a 'one model, one modality' paradigm for visual reasoning. While not positioned to replace text tokenizers everywhere, it serves as a powerful diagnostic tool that challenges our assumptions about the need for separate, heterogeneous representations in multimodal systems. The key takeaway is that with the right training-time guidance, complex reasoning can emerge from what is fundamentally a pixel-to-pixel transformation.
segments.zh: 总结一下，OCG 提出了一种“一个模型、一种模态”的视觉推理范式。虽然它并非旨在在所有场景下取代文本 tokenizer，但它是一个强有力的诊断工具，挑战了我们对多模态系统中是否需要分离的、异构表示的假设。关键结论是，有了正确的训练时引导，复杂的推理可以从本质上只是像素到像素的变换中涌现出来。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 感谢收听。如果还有任何问题，可以问我们的人工智能助手，或者留言评论。
